want.who_she_is: Rilla Vance, 27, nee Marek. Eleven weeks married to Dorn Vance, 54, who owns Vance Diesel — a repair yard on a county road outside Kerr Crossing, house on the same gravel lot. A paper signed before the wedding: nothing is hers for three years. No car in her name, not on the account, sixty dollars a week on the kitchen counter. Dorn put her on the books, so she writes down every number the yard makes and can touch none of them, and hands the week's cash to his eldest son on Friday. Dorn hauls four nights out of seven. What she has to lose: the three years, and the job she got her brother.
want.appetite: To be wanted by men who have to call her by a title she did not earn. It cannot complete — no figure of respect settles it, and every man who starts using her name has to be replaced by one still using the title. The yard supplies them: drivers, hires, family home from somewhere. Release 41 adds a new hire in the bunk room, a customer who becomes a regular, or another Vance who needs a bed.
want.ascent: Bottom: the office counter and the front rooms of the house, in daylight, with Dorn's name doing all the work; she asks Cade for the truck to leave the property at all. Top: the shop floor after close, the bunk room over it, the wash bay at midnight, the sleepers in the back row — and none of it needing his name, because by then they are not calling her by it. The ladders live on the cast: five men, two meters each (access — what he lets her near; willingness — how far he goes).

why_this_person.npc_cade: Cade Vance, 29. Runs the yard, two years older than his stepmother. He never once pretended the marriage was normal, and he decides what she is allowed to touch.
why_this_person.npc_isaac: Isaac Vance, 24. Bunk room over the shop. He watches and says nothing, and being watched by him was the first thing about this place she liked.
why_this_person.npc_booth: Booth Vance, 19. Still in the house. The only one who takes the title at face value and means it — and undoing that is the whole taboo.
why_this_person.npc_sherrod: Sherrod Vance, 51. Dorn's brother, lives over the office. He arranged this, more or less, and has never said what he thinks he is owed.
why_this_person.npc_tobin: Tobin Marek, 22. Her brother, and she got him the job. The only person alive who knew her before the title, and the only one who can say out loud what she married into.
why_this_person.npc_dorn: Dorn Vance, 54. The husband. He is the clock and not a hub: three nights his truck is in the lot and four nights it is not, and the whole week is which.

2026-08-27 — THE MONEY NOW BUYS SOMETHING, AND THE OBLIGATION MOVES. REVIEW.md E1. E1 asked one question: the week earns roughly four times the 260 rent, should 260 go up? The research pass (~/Documents/Economy_Pressure_Study_20260827/, 19 field games + our ten) answered NO, and the number was not the finding. THREE MEASUREMENTS DECIDED THIS. (1) Their money buys content; ours bought meter points — seven corpus games sell a person, a scene or an unlock (degrees-of-lewdity's Robin, patriarch's Lilith behind Villa Garcia, corpo-life's marriage behind a 1M apartment), and this game's five purchases bought clean +45, standing +4/+5/+6 and trust +3/+4, with ZERO of its 55 trait conditions reading money. (2) Squeezing harder is the corpus's most-punished move — the two games that made money bite are the two whose players are angriest and one dev is on record walking it back; the decisive comment is four words, 'here u still grind for nothing'. (3) The field's obligation MOVES and ours is a build-time constant (setup.rent_amount, v2.py:3118), so it goes soft at whatever value it is set to. LO'S FOUR CALLS: all three layers · the sink is a truck in Tobin's name · the weekly number rises because of the truck's RUNNING COSTS (sluttown-usa's $serverRent = $runningServers * 50, not degrees-of-lewdity's imposed ratchet — DoL gates NOTHING on $rentstage and gets away with a bare rise because Bailey is a believed predator; here the Friday money is already the yard's, so a number that climbs on its own reads as the author turning a dial) · income scales with the obligation. BUILT: ask_papers @ the_bank (its FIRST affordance — the room had three canvases and all three were random ambients) → the ask on hub_tobin_shop, gated `money gte 2600`, which is the beat that makes money gate content → see_truck @ kerr_crossing, a four-band ladder reading the drawer and a 2600 purchase. Upkeep -22/day on [engine.daily_tick] traitEffects gated `truck_bought`, which NOTIFIES (setup.applyAndNotifyTrait, v2.py:5586) rather than draining silently — a silent charge meter is the one economy device the corpus universally hates (sluttown-usa). The parts run pays 125 instead of 34 with her own truck, no key off Cade's board: course-of-temptation denominates its payouts in the debt itself (_cash = Math.floor($weeklydebt * 0.15)) so a rising number is a difficulty curve and never more clicking; our engine has no computed effect values, so the same thing is done with a band. Week: +455 from the run against -154 upkeep = +301 net, obligation 260 → 414. And `cade_covered` stopped being a dead flag — set by the engine, read by NOTHING, two hits in the merged game. Now a band on hub_cade_office, a rung that only exists once the debt does, and an ASK gated `money lt 260`. ⚠️ NO ENGINE CHANGE WAS NEEDED and the staged-rent feature was deliberately NOT built: daily_tick traitEffects already take a per-effect condition gate (template_import.py:706), and a DoL-style stage array would make the sidebar `max = 260` and the quest goal `money gte 260` both lie. The daily upkeep leaves Friday at 260, so both surfaces stay true. ⚠️ The +260 Cade grant carries the THREE-PART DAY CAP on one choice (reads cade_rung_today is_false, sets it, daily_tick clears it) plus `cade_covered is_false`, which is what keeps it off gate 18 — _holder_day_capped excludes a self-capped holder from _grants. ⚠️ kerr_crossing and the_bank fills RE-DECLARED (300→620, 500→660) because the design moved, not to clear the gate; the reason is written beside each in board.locations[].fill_note. VERIFIED LIVE in headless Chromium (playtest_economy.py, new): 14/14 — the four bands render exactly one arm each, every new rung is CLICKABLE only in its own state, and the upkeep takes 22 off the drawer on advanceDay() with the truck and 0 without. ⚠️ The first run of that harness reported two false failures by asserting on TEXT: a cost-blocked choice renders as Buy it. ($2600, 1h) (Requires 2600 Money (you have 2599)), so the label is on screen while the player cannot click it. 2026-08-28 — STUDY 8: THE TRUCK TURNS OUT TO BE THE HOUSE'S ONLY OWNED ASSET, AND NOW THERE IS A GATE THAT SAYS SO. Study 8 (~/Documents/Accumulation_Study_20260828/, 25 corpus games, ~55,000 passages) measured it. 2026-08-28 — B2: THE RELEASE BOUNDARY BECOMES AN INSTRUMENT. No file in this game changed; this records what was built at the skill layer off this game's REVIEW and what it found. LO's call, after B2 was explained. THE DEFECT: LO's rule — dev mode and missing media block RELEASE, not testing — was correct and held by nothing. It lived as a comment on a JS object literal (games-data.js:44-49), hand-copied into nine of twenty-eight portal entries in three wordings. gates.py had ZERO lines reading a built game (its only knowledge of dev mode was a TOML trigger marker at :2621-2627) and the-release.md — 164 lines, 8 headings, named for this — never mentioned --dev, --debug, a placeholder or a build. All 43 gates measure 7_final_game.toml, which is structurally incapable of judging an artefact, and a release is the one moment the artefact is what is judged. THE CORRECTION, shipped with the claim: B2 itself specified failing on an [IMAGE MISSING] / [VIDEO POOL MISSING] marker in the built HTML. Those markers are --debug ONLY (v2.py:12403 'if not self.debug: return \'\'', :14753, :14903), so a clean build renders SILENT gaps and the grep passes it — under_one_roof ships a clean build with 183 missing files and zero markers. The check reads the build's own flags-init map instead (debug_mode at v2.py:1077, dev_mode_enabled at :1081-1082) plus MissingMediaPage, which v2.py:216 documents as 'always generated, but button only shows in debug mode'. colour_meter.shape: W5b audience meter - it RISES, it almost never refuses, and as of 2026-08-27 it DELIVERS PEOPLE (patriarch's shape). Deliberately GLOBAL, not scoped per place.
colour_meter.what: how much of the Vance name is actually hers. Rises when a man treats her as his father's wife in front of someone; falls when he treats her as something else in front of someone.
colour_meter.note: Read to swap a line - the driver at the counter who talks to her or asks for a man, the clerk's tone, what the bar already knows - AND to decide who walks in. W5b: it rises and it RARELY refuses; do NOT apply W5's shuts-a-door test, W5 owns the meter that closes and W5b the meter that talks. CORRECTED 2026-08-27: the old '644 read sites, refuses at 2%' figure is three games (95% degrees-of-lewdity) and is withdrawn. Re-measured over 13 field games: ~10% of branch arms carry a link, and a MEDIAN 41% of reads change something mechanical - by delivering people (patriarch), modifying a roll (destroyer) or scaling a rate (corpo-life). Rarely-refuses survives; only-swaps-a-line does not. BUILT 2026-08-27 (S1b): below standing 40 the four NAMELESS walk-ins fire more often - walkin_office_driver 0.30 to 0.45, walkin_bay_seen 0.20 to 0.35, walkin_shop_watched 0.25 to 0.40, walkin_row_cab 0.25 to 0.40. The five NAMED walk-ins run on trust and want and are untouched: they are relationships, not an audience. Direction is deliberate - WANT.md §4 makes the fantasy the title being stripped, so high standing buys respect at the counter and costs traffic in the yard, and nothing is locked at any value. Rules are APPENDED to their exclusive_group, never prepended: group rules share one dice over cumulative buckets (v2.py:5345) and a claimed-but-failed slot falls to solo rather than promoting the next rule (v2.py:5378), so an appended rule takes a bucket that already fell to solo and at gte 40 nothing changes. Reads 4 -> 22, in 1 canvas -> 6. See REVIEW.md S1a and S1b.

locations.job: The ground the whole world sits on - gravel between the house and the shop, opening onto the county road. Where anyone can see anything.
She keeps the books here because Dorn told her to. Cade signs, drivers come to the counter, and it sits between the house and the shop - the one room both worlds touch.
Four bays and a parts wall. Where the work is and where the men are all day.
Concrete, a drain, a hose on a reel, and no door. Where trucks get washed and where she gets clean when the house is full.
Over the shop. Two beds, a window on the yard. Isaac lives here and so does her brother.
Where overnight trucks park, each with a bed behind the seats. The far end of the property and the last place anybody looks.
Up the outside stairs over the office. He has been here longer than the marriage and he has never said what he thinks he is owed.
The back door of the house opens into it. Where the family is a family, three nights a week.
Hers and Dorn's, and his four nights of the week. Where the day ends.
One bathroom, five adults, a bolt that does not sit in its keeper.
The youngest one's room, and the only one in the house who still means the title.
The crossroads twenty minutes down the road. Pumps, a light, the flatbed on the end of the lot, and the only place on earth nobody here owns.
locations.fill_note: RE-DECLARED 2026-08-27 (E1), from 300. Not a number moved to match delivery: the design changed. The crossing now carries the game's aspirational sink - the flatbed, its four-band ladder that reads the drawer, and the purchase scene - because the field's warmly-discussed economies all put the big purchase somewhere the player passes long before affording it. A budget re-declared when the plan changes is the plan; a budget re-declared to clear a gate is the fudge the-board.md exists to prevent.

economy.obligation_moves: the truck's fuel and plates - 22 a day, every day, from the morning she buys it (2600, in Tobin's name). 260 on Friday never changes; the week does, 260 -> 414. Cost follows holdings (the-economy.md R3b, sluttown-usa's shape) rather than an imposed ratchet, because the Friday money is already the yard's and a number that climbed on its own would read as the author turning a dial. The parts run pays 125 instead of 34 with her own truck, so the income moves with it (R3c).
economy.week_income_note: What a five-day week actually pays before the truck: counter 74 + trailer 62 + parts run 34 + books 22 + walk-round 16 = 208/day, all five day-capped, x5 weekdays. Energy is the real ceiling - the five rungs cost 72 and one sleep restores 70 - so 1040 is the honest maximum, not the expected. Declared here because the-economy.md R3 says to price the obligation against the income in BOTH directions and nine of our ten games did not: the one that did (forty_miles) wrote the sum in a prose comment, because the ledger gave it nowhere to live. Ratio: 260/1040 = 25% before the truck, 414/1495 = 28% after (the haul lifts the week to 1495 and the upkeep takes 154). forty_miles, the only one of ten in the field's range, runs 70%.
economy.note: The reversal, mechanised: she holds the drawer and is not on the account. Short on Friday and Cade covers it - eviction_mode = flag_set sets `cade_covered`, a debt to Cade. Money failure feeds the cast meters instead of ending the game. ⚠️ THIS NOTE SAID `and opens his ladder` UNTIL 2026-08-27 AND IT WAS FALSE: the flag was set by the engine and read by nothing, two hits in the whole merged game. It is now read by a band on hub_cade_office and by a rung that only exists once the debt does, and she can ASK for it before Friday (money lt 260) instead of only arriving at it by neglect - degrees-of-lewdity's `$robinpaid`, where taking on a debt doubles the rent and buys a love interest.
